{{pagebanner|Mena-asia_default_banner.jpg|pgname=Eastern Tokyo|caption=Tokyo Sea Life Park at Kasai}}
[[File:TokyoEast.png|thumb|250px|Eastern wards of Tokyo]]
'''Eastern Tokyo''' covers the wards of '''Adachi''' (足立), '''Katsushika''' (葛飾), '''Edogawa''' (江戸川), '''Kōtō''' (江東) and '''Arakawa''' (荒川).  Neighboring '''[[Tokyo/Sumida|Sumida]]''' (墨田) is covered in its own article, as is the flashy bayside shopping and entertainment district of '''[[Tokyo/Odaiba|Odaiba]]'''.

==Understand==
Eastern Tokyo is largely residential and industrial. The one major attraction here is the new Toyosu Market, the world's largest fish market famed for its tuna auctions, which replaced the old Tsukiji Market in 2018.

===Tourist Information Sites===
(from north to south)
*Adachi: [https://www.adachikanko.net/ Local tourist association], with integrated machine translation.
*Arakawa: [https://www.city.arakawa.tokyo.jp/foreign/en/index.html ArakawAmazing!] is the ward's official multilingual guide site.
*Katsushika: [https://katsushika-kanko.jp/index.html Local tourist association], Japanese-only.
*Edogawa:The ward's official website has [https://www.city.edogawa.tokyo.jp/sports/kankomidokoro/index.html a multilingual tourism section].
*Kōtō: [https://koto-kanko.jp/ Local tourist association], with integrated machine translation.

==Get in==
===By rail===

To Adachi: Tobu Skytree Line, Umejima Station or Gotanno Station.

To Koiwa: Chuo-Sobu from Shinjuku and Akihabara in the west or Chiba outside of Tokyo.

* {{see
| name=Toyosu Market | alt=豊洲市場 Toyosu Shijō | url=https://www.toyosu-market.or.jp/en/ | email=
| address=6 Toyosu, Koto-ku | lat=35.644167 | long=139.783611 | directions=Shijō-mae Station on the Yurikamome Line
| phone=+81 3-3520-8205 | tollfree=
| hours=M-Sa 05:00-17:00; closed holidays and most Wednesdays | price=Free
| wikipedia=Toyosu Market | image=Toyosu_fish_market-4b.jpg | wikidata=Q11633916
| lastedit=2019-02-12
| content=Toyosu is new home of the world's largest wholesale market for seafood and produce after its relocation from [[Tokyo/Chuo#See|Tsukiji]]. Unlike the old facility where tourists could almost walk up to the fish, Toyosu's market has large enclosed observation decks and dedicated paths for tourists to view the action, including the famous tuna auctions. However, early morning fish sales start before public transit opens, so take a taxi for those.
}}<p>A [https://www.shijou.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/english/pamphlet/ pamphlet showing the visitors' course]{{Dead link|date=March 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} outlines the three buildings. The Wholesale Market Building is where fish are auctioned to intermediate brokers. Many of those are located in the Intermediate Wholesale Building, where they peddle to resellers and restaurants (but not the general public). In the Fruits and Vegetables Building, a similar tiered structure sells produce, meat, and flowers.</p><p>'''Fish auctions''' start at 05:00 and run roughly 1 hour, sometimes less; you should arrive early to get a good view. Other auctions follow until around 08:00. Most of the market activity is done by 11:00, after which it becomes a bit of a ghost town until the next morning. Visitors are separated from the market in upstairs viewing galleries, and it's still impressive even though you can't hear or smell anything through the glass. For the tuna auction, 120 people per day can observe from a bottom-floor observation deck, from which you ''can'' hear the auctioneers' chant. Tickets are granted by '''lottery'''; you must apply online or by phone in the first half of the month that precedes your desired visit (which means between 3-7 weeks in advance).</p><p>On the roof, a minimalist grass deck offers good views of Tokyo Bay. While you can't enter the lower markets, there are many dozens of '''shops and eateries''' where you can sample some sushi or purchase a persimmon; however, if you want to get face to face with a fish, visit the many shops in [[Tokyo/Chuo#See|Tsukiji's outer market]] instead.</p>

* {{see
| name=Fukagawa Edo Museum | alt=深川江戸資料館, fukagawa edo shiryōkan | url=https://www.kcf.or.jp/fukagawa/ | email=
| address=1-3-28 Shirakawa, Kōtō-ku | lat=35.68092 | long=139.8007 | directions=10 min from Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Station on the Toei Ōedo and Hanzōmon lines; from Exit A3, turn left; at the next traffic light, turn left again; the museum is ahead on the left, past the entrance to a temple
| phone=+81 3-3630-8625 | tollfree= | fax=+81 3-3820-4379
| hours= | price=&yen;300 adult
| image=Fukagawa Edo Museum.JPG | wikidata=Q3090685
| content=This intimate museum features a wonderfully recreated Tempo-period (1830-1843) neighbourhood - complete with homes, shops, narrow alleyways, and even the local rubbish dump. Wander about, peering in windows and entering buildings furnished with household goods and Edo-period bric-a-brac. Light and sound effects create the illusion of a whole day passing from day to night in the space of a few minutes. Pair it up with a visit to the huge [[Tokyo/Sumida#Edo-Tokyo Museum|Edo-Tokyo Museum]] in nearby Sumida ward, just a couple of stops away on the Toei Ōedo subway line.
}}
* {{see
| name=Shibamata | alt=柴又 | url= | email=
| address= | lat=35.758597 | long=139.878247 | directions=
| phone= | tollfree=
| hours= | price=
| image=Shibamata street.jpg | wikidata=Q11534647
| content=In Katsushika-ku, it features '''Taishakuten Temple''' (帝釈天) with its cozy shopping street that rivals [[Asakusa]] in liveliness while being much more authentic, lacking the overseas-tourist kitsch. The district's biggest claim to fame is being the setting for "Otoko wa tsurai yo", Japan's longest-running movie series, and the hero of the series, '''Tora-san''', can be seen every block of the way from the life-size statue in front of the train station to caricatures and movie posters in every shop. Down by the river past the temple there is a museum dedicated to the movie series, as well as a hand-rowed boat that carries passengers between the shores (¥100 one way fare), the last of its kind in Tokyo. You might want to cover the [http://www.shibamata.jp/sevengods/s_godmap.html 7 gods], a series of temples around the neighbourhood, get a free map at the station.
}}

* {{see
| name=Kasai Rinkai Park | alt=葛西臨海公園 | url= | email=
| address= | lat=35.64286 | long=139.86257 | directions=next to Kasai Rinkai Koen Station on the JR Keiyo Line, 10-15 minutes and ¥210 from Tokyo Station; the platforms of the Keiyo Line at Tokyo Station are a 10-minute walk from the station's other platforms
| phone=+81 3-5696-1331 | tollfree=
| hours= | price=Free
| wikipedia=Kasai Rinkai Park | image=Kasai-Rinkai-Park View Plaza Rest House.jpg | wikidata=Q1038727
| lastedit=2025-11-17
| content=The largest park in central Tokyo is just across the Edogawa River from [[Tokyo Disney Resort]]. Opened in 1989, the park was built on reclaimed land and developed in an effort to restore and preserve natural Tokyo Bay habitat. The park offers a nice break from the surrounding cityscapes and has a number of walking trails that crisscross the gardens, lawns and beaches. In addition, the park features an aquarium, two cafes, a Ferris wheel, a seabird sanctuary, and the Crystal View observatory. Mt Fuji is viewable on a clear day from the Ferris Wheel and the observatory. There are a number of ferries (waterbuses) that serve the park though these services are infrequent and announced in advance on the [https://www.tokyo-park.or.jp/water/waterbus/ Tokyo Parks Waterbus] page.
}}

==Eat==
[[File:Monjayaki.jpg|thumb|Monja-yaki]]
"''Monja-yaki''" (もんじゃ焼き) is a [[Kanto]]-area specialty, similar to ''okonomiyaki''. Once people used to draw letters with ingredients on the hot plate for fun before eating because "Monja-yaki" means "letter cake". Monja-yaki's basic batter is made of water, flour and soy sauce. Ingredients can include cabbage, grated yam, crushed ''tempura'', cuttlefish, shrimp, slices of meat, and so on. Although [[Tokyo/Chuo|Tsukishima]] is Tokyo's best-known neighborhood for monjayaki, it's popular here as well.

* {{sleep
| name=Hotel Lumiere Nishikasai | alt= | url=https://www.hotel-lumiere.jp/nishikasai/en/ | email=
| address=6-20-3 Nishikasai, Edogawa-ku | lat=35.66239 | long=139.86132 | directions=
| phone=+81 03 5676 2711 | tollfree=
| checkin=15:00 | checkout=10:00 | price=
| lastedit=2025-11-17
| content=A comfortable 3-star hotel located within 5 minutes walk of Nishikasai station on the Tozai Line (20 mins to Tokyo Station, one transfer to Asakusa, Akihabara, Shinjuku). Airport Limousine buses run to the nearby Kasai Station (15 mins walk or one stop on the Tozai Line). The rooms are larger than a standard business hotel with some including a washer/dryer combo and a small kitchenette. The hotel has free amenities such as bathroom items (razor, toothbrush, face cream, bath scents), a coffee machine available 24/7 in reception, and a modern room TV allowing Netflix and Youtube to be used. A small buffet is available each morning with simple foods (breads, fruit, eggs, and 1-2 cooked dishes) and a drink selection (coffee, teas, juices). The staff will assist with holding luggage before check-in and organised luggage forwarding. On the upper floors there are nice views including the Kasai Rinkai Park Ferris Wheel, the Skytree, and the Disneyland fireworks show, on a clear day you can see Mt Fuji through the Tokyo Skyline. There is plenty of nearby food options and a decent playground for kids.
}}
